text:
Agentic Attack Detections

 
 
 

Open-source detection rules, hunting queries and indicators for security teams. They cover agentic attack frameworks: tools that hand an intrusion to AI agents, which plan, run real attack tools and keep going until they reach a goal.

Free to use under the MIT license. Fixes, false-positive reports and new indicators are welcome.

 What is here

- Framework folders. ARTEX and its AntiFox fork, Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, CyberStrikeAI, Strix, Hermes Agent and Agent Zero. Each folder is built from a review of the framework's source code and the public reporting on its use.
- Shared behaviors. Rules for what these frameworks have in common, whatever the tool or the model behind it.
- Indicators and feeds. One CSV of 516 sourced indicators, and the feeds generated from it.

Formats: KQL for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR, Sigma, Suricata, Zeek, YARA and STIX 2.1, plus WAF rules for Cloudflare, AWS WAF and Azure WAF. Splunk and Elastic are covered by a Splunk app and Elastic rules for ARTEX, and by Sigma conversions for everything else.

 Start here

 You have Do this 
 --- --- 
 Microsoft Sentinel Upload feeds/sentinel-watchlist.csv as a watchlist with the alias AGENTIC IOCs and the search key value . Import the analytics rules from frameworks/ /sentinel/analytics/ and behaviors/sentinel/analytics/ . Run the hunts in each folder's hunting-order.md order 
 Defender XDR Run the hunts from frameworks/ /sentinel/hunting/ in advanced hunting. They work where the tables exist 
 Suricata Add the .rules files from frameworks/ /suricata/ and behaviors/suricata/ . HTTP rules need cleartext or decrypted traffic. DNS and TLS SNI rules work on encrypted traffic 
 Zeek Install the behaviors package with zkg install (or load behaviors/zeek/agentic-behaviors/ by path), set server nets to your server ranges (setup), load frameworks/artex/zeek/artex/ , and feed frameworks/ /zeek/intel/ .intel to the Intel framework 
 YARA Scan container layers, home folders, /tmp and web roots with frameworks/ /yara/ 
 Any SIEM with Sigma Convert frameworks/ /sigma/ and behaviors/sigma/ with sigma convert , or take the conversions in generated/ 
 Splunk or Elastic The ARTEX folder has a Splunk app and Elastic rules. For the other frameworks use generated/ 
 A WAF: Cloudflare, AWS WAF or Azure WAF Deploy the rules in waf/ : framework user agents, probe markers and unsigned JWT probes to block, and reported addresses to challenge. A WAF is optional. It adds blocking at the edge to the detections, it doesn't replace them 
 A threat intelligence platform Import feeds/stix2.1-bundle.json , or the per-framework lists in feeds/by-framework/

Suricata counts are hand-written rules; each framework also has address rules generated from its indicators. Some indicators belong to more than one framework. ARTEX also has a Splunk app, Elastic rules and ES\ QL queries, and an osquery pack.

 Frameworks

 Framework What it is Seen in 
 --- --- --- 
 ARTEX Go planner and worker agents with a web console. AntiFox is the same code renamed Storm-0940, Storm-3358, VAPOR PANDA and criminal groups, against Microsoft 365, Okta, AWS, Azure, web applications and Active Directory 
 Cairn Python engine that drives Claude Code, Codex and Pi coding agents in Kali containers Online retailers, payment sites, Japanese web applications and WSUS servers 
 PentAGI Go multi-agent platform that runs Kali tools in a container per engagement Intrusions GTIG and Mandiant reported since August 2026, and a PaperCut exploitation operator's infrastructure 
 HexStrike Python MCP server that gives any AI assistant about 150 security tools over an unauthenticated API NetScaler exploitation discussion in 2025, and intrusions GTIG and Mandiant reported 
 CyberStrikeAI Go operator console whose agents run about 90 tools, with its own implants, C2 listeners and webshell manager FortiGate mass-exploitation infrastructure, an AWS intrusion, and education organizations in Africa and Latin America 
 Strix Python AI pentest agent that runs teams of agents in a Kali sandbox, on any model The retail card-theft campaign Gambit reported, where it found the flaws Cairn exploited 
 Hermes Agent A legitimate general-purpose agent turned into an attack console: approvals off, a bundled jailbreak skill, red-team personas The Gambit retail operator, the Carbonato Docker botnet, and Thailand's Ministry of Finance 
 Agent Zero General-purpose agent in a Kali container with a built-in hacker profile and an open web UI Threat-actor experimentation GTIG reported, with no published indicators 

Each folder has a README, the hunts and rules, and a source-code-signals.md that explains what the framework leaves behind and where in its code each signal comes from.

 Behaviors shared by agentic frameworks

 behaviors/ holds rules that do not depend on any one framework.

 Behavior Rules 
 --- --- 
 An attack tool started under an AI agent CLI (Claude Code, Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, Codex, opencode, Hermes, Cairn's workers), found from the process tree KQL hunt, Sentinel analytics rule, Sigma 
 Servers calling AI model APIs: Chinese models (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Doubao), gateways such as OpenRouter, and Western APIs KQL hunt, Sigma, Zeek
